dedupe_keys.name: space weather effects chronology natural resources canada

description: This Government of Canada page, part of the Natural Resources Canada space weather site, is a chronology of documented effects of geomagnetic disturbances on technological systems, above all electrical power systems, pipelines, telegraph lines and communications cables. Entries are arranged by year and give the date of the disturbance, the affected system and a description of the effect, each with citations to historical sources and scientific papers. Coverage runs from 1847, with early telegraph disruptions, to 2004, with roughly fifty or more incidents worldwide and a North American emphasis; the March 1989 entry, for example, records the collapse of Hydro-Québec's 21,000 MW grid in 25 seconds after seven static var compensators tripped, and a nine-hour blackout. It was compiled to document the geomagnetic hazard to infrastructure and was last modified on 1 March 2019. The chronology is accessible online as a free HTML page on spaceweather.gc.ca under the Government of Canada's standard terms, with no download file or API. Caveats: it is a curated narrative list, not a structured database, it stops in 2004, and entries are uneven in detail. It supports historical event analysis and hazard exposure studies of space weather on power grids and pipelines; related records are the SuperMAG and OMNIWeb data and the Hydro-Québec March 1989 blackout case study.
